name: Lie groups were invented to integrate ODEs
summary: Sophus Lie built the theory of continuous groups in the 1870s to do for differential equations what Galois theory did for polynomials. Each one-parameter point symmetry lowers an ODE's order by one, and symmetry reductions of PDEs give similarity solutions and separable coordinates. The algebraic core of that programme became the Lie theory physics uses today.

name: CODATA uncertainties, correlations and exact constants
summary: CODATA values carry standard uncertainties plus a correlation matrix, because many constants derive from shared inputs. Since 2019 h, e, k and N_A are exact, so their former uncertainty now sits in μ0, ε0, the molar mass constant and the mass of the old prototype kilogram.

name: Molecular dynamics integrates Hamilton's equations
summary: Microcanonical MD integrates Hamilton's equations for N particles numerically. Nosé's extended Hamiltonian adds a thermostat variable s, so the deterministic Hamiltonian flow samples the canonical ensemble in real variables, assuming the extended system is ergodic.

name: Finite elements born in structural elasticity
summary: The finite element method grew out of structural and elasticity analysis (Courant's 1943 variational triangles, 1950s aircraft stress analysis) and is a Ritz–Galerkin minimization of the elastic energy.

name: Floquet theory of the Mathieu equation
summary: Parametric resonance is governed by Floquet–Hill theory of linear ODEs with periodic coefficients; Mathieu characteristic exponents define the instability tongues near ω = 2ω₀/n.

name: Normal modes = generalized eigenproblem
summary: Small oscillations about equilibrium reduce to the symmetric generalized eigenproblem Kv = ω²Mv; normal modes are the orthogonal eigenvectors guaranteed by the spectral theorem.

name: Fictitious forces as connection coefficients
summary: In Newton–Cartan form, with time as a coordinate, the Coriolis and centrifugal forces in a rotating frame are the connection coefficients Γ^i_{0j} and Γ^i_{00}. Free motion becomes a geodesic of a flat spacetime connection, which prefigures the equivalence principle.
map: \ddot x^i+\Gamma^i_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu\dot x^\nu=F^i/m,\ x^0=t;\ \Gamma^i_{0j}=\epsilon_{ijk}... \Rightarrow -2\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf v,\ \Gamma^i_{00}\Rightarrow\boldsymbol\Omega\times(\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf r)

name: Re ≪ 1 regime and the scallop theorem
summary: At Re ≪ 1 inertia drops out and Stokes flow is linear and instantaneous, so reciprocal strokes give no net swimming (Purcell's scallop theorem); scaling arguments set what microswimmers can do.

name: Ewald summation: electrostatics on a periodic lattice
summary: Periodic simulations need the Coulomb energy of an infinite lattice of images, a conditionally convergent sum. Ewald splits 1/r into a short-range erfc part summed in real space and a smooth part summed in Fourier space. The leftover surface-dipole term depends on the dielectric condition at infinity; tin-foil boundaries (ε'=∞) are the usual choice.

name: Monte Carlo radiative transfer through turbid media
summary: Multiple scattering of light in clouds, tissue and dust is simulated as random walks of photon packets. Free paths are drawn from the extinction coefficient and scattering angles from a Mie or Henyey–Greenstein phase function. This solves the radiative transfer equation statistically where the diffusion approximation fails.

name: Split-step Fourier solution of the fibre NLSE
summary: Pulse propagation in a Kerr fibre obeys the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, solved by operator splitting. Dispersion is applied exactly in the Fourier domain and self-phase modulation in the time domain; Strang splitting makes the scheme second order. This norm-preserving pseudospectral method also underlies Lugiato–Lefever simulations of Kerr combs and solitons.

name: Electrodynamics of moving bodies gave special relativity
summary: Einstein's 1905 paper opens with the magnet–conductor asymmetry of Maxwell–Lorentz electrodynamics. He resolved it by making the Lorentz transformations, which already leave Maxwell's equations invariant, the kinematics of space and time. Minkowski's 1908 tensor form then made E and B frame-dependent parts of one object, so relativity grew out of electrodynamics rather than mechanics.

name: Statics as Poisson problems for V and A
summary: Electrostatics, and magnetostatics in Coulomb gauge, both reduce to Poisson equations: one for V and one for each Cartesian component of A. Coulomb's law and the Biot–Savart law are therefore both the sources convolved with the same Green's function 1/(4πr).
map: \nabla^2V=-\rho/\epsilon_0,\ \nabla^2\mathbf A=-\mu_0\mathbf J\Rightarrow\mathbf A=\mu_0\int G\,\mathbf J\,d^3r',\ G=\frac{1}{4\pi|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}

name: Coulomb potential as the Laplacian's Green's function
summary: The point-charge potential is the free-space Green's function of the Laplacian. Dirichlet and Neumann Green's functions, the method of images and separation of variables (via Sturm–Liouville completeness) are the general PDE tools applied to conductors. Uniqueness follows from the elliptic type of the problem.

name: T-breaking and absent Kramers protection for photons
summary: Photonic Chern insulators with one-way edge modes need broken time reversal, from gyromagnetic or time-modulated media. Photons are bosons with Θ²=+1, so they lack the Kramers degeneracy that protects electronic Z₂ topological insulators. Photonic 'quantum spin Hall' analogues instead use engineered pseudo-spins, which symmetry-breaking defects can couple.

name: Multipole moments as irreducible SO(3) tensors
summary: The 2l+1 spherical moments of order l form an irreducible representation of the rotation group, so a rank-l Cartesian moment reduces to its symmetric traceless part. The Wigner–Eckart theorem then gives the selection rules for multipole radiation. It also forbids moments of order l>2j in a state of angular momentum j, so a spin-½ particle has no quadrupole moment.

name: Plasma frequency as photon mass: Anderson's Higgs route
summary: In a collisionless Drude medium, transverse light obeys ω²=ω_p²+c²k², a massive Klein–Gordon dispersion. The long-range Coulomb force lifts the would-be acoustic density mode to the plasmon at ω_p. Anderson used this plasma picture to argue that a gauge field can gain mass by absorbing a would-be Goldstone mode, the core of the Higgs–Anderson mechanism.
breaks: A normal plasma has no condensate and no broken symmetry. A collisionless plasma only freezes in static magnetic flux, like a perfect conductor, while a superconductor expels it (Meissner effect) because its photon mass comes from a phase-coherent condensate. With collisions, static fields penetrate fully.

name: Laser threshold as spontaneous U(1) phase breaking
summary: Near threshold the single-mode field amplitude obeys a Landau-like equation. Below threshold only zero field is stable; above it there is a ring of states with fixed amplitude and arbitrary phase. The phase is then a Goldstone-like soft mode, and its diffusion under spontaneous-emission noise sets the Schawlow–Townes linewidth.
breaks: A laser is an open, driven-dissipative system rather than an equilibrium ground state. A single mode is effectively zero-dimensional, so the phase diffuses freely (finite linewidth). There is no true long-range order or thermodynamic singularity, only a crossover that sharpens with photon number.

name: Ampere redefinition: μ0 became a measured constant
summary: Until 2019 the ampere was defined by the magnetostatic force between parallel wires, which fixed μ0=4π×10⁻⁷ N A⁻² exactly. Fixing e and h instead makes μ0 a measured quantity tied to the fine-structure constant. CODATA 2022 gives μ0=1.256 637 061 27(20)×10⁻⁶ N A⁻², within 1σ of the old exact value.

name: H-theorem and the Loschmidt–Zermelo objections
summary: Boltzmann's H-theorem derives monotonic entropy increase from the Boltzmann equation. Loschmidt raised the reversal objection and Zermelo the recurrence objection. In the replies (Burbury, Boltzmann, the Ehrenfests) the time asymmetry was traced to the molecular-chaos assumption (Stosszahlansatz). This is now the standard case of irreversibility emerging from reversible laws.

name: Canonical energy fluctuations limit microcalorimeters
summary: A microcalorimeter or bolometer weakly linked to a bath has canonical energy fluctuations $\langle\Delta E^2\rangle=k_BT^2C$. This thermodynamic-fluctuation noise sets the ultimate resolution of transition-edge sensors, which is why they operate near 0.1 K with tiny heat capacity.

name: Kelvin redefined by fixing the Boltzmann constant
summary: Thermodynamic temperature, defined through the second law by Kelvin's Carnot scale, has since 2019 been defined by fixing k_B exactly. The fixed value came from primary thermometry based on statistical mechanics: acoustic gas thermometry (u²=γk_BT/m), dielectric-constant gas thermometry and Johnson-noise thermometry, which now also realize the kelvin alongside ITS-90.

name: Eigenproblems and special functions of quantum mechanics
summary: Separation of variables, Sturm–Liouville eigenproblems and orthogonal polynomials (Hermite, Laguerre, Legendre) give the textbook spectra. Green's functions, contour integrals and asymptotic methods underpin perturbation theory, scattering and WKB.

name: Spectral theorem as the measurement postulate
summary: States are rays in a Hilbert space and observables are self-adjoint operators. The spectral theorem supplies the possible outcomes (eigenvalues) and the projectors that the Born rule and state update use. Gleason's theorem shows that in dimension ≥ 3 every noncontextual, additive probability measure on projectors has the form Tr(ρP).

name: Cryogenic sensors as single-photon detectors
summary: Cryogenic sensors and the noise analysis of instrumentation have become quantum-optics hardware. Transition-edge sensors resolve photon number with about 95% efficiency. Superconducting nanowire detectors have reached about 98% efficiency in some devices and few-picosecond jitter in others. Dark counts and dead time are the other figures of merit.

name: Rotation symmetry labels states and selection rules
summary: Rotational invariance of H makes j and m good quantum numbers. The Wigner–Eckart theorem splits every tensor-operator matrix element into a Clebsch–Gordan coefficient times a reduced element, which gives the dipole selection rules.

name: Atomic parity violation and electron EDM searches
summary: Z-boson exchange mixes S and P states, so the forbidden Cs 6S–7S transition gains a parity-odd amplitude that measures the weak charge Q_W (Wood et al. 1997). Electron-EDM searches in heavy atoms and polar molecules test T, and hence CP, violation; the best bound is |d_e| < 4.1×10^{-30} e·cm (JILA HfF+, 2023).

name: Kramers degeneracy from T² = −1 for half-integer spin
summary: Time reversal is antiunitary and acts on spin as Θ = e^{-iπS_y/ħ}K, so Θ² = (−1)^{2S}. With an odd number of electrons, every level is at least doubly degenerate unless a magnetic field breaks T. This is the origin of the protected Kramers pairs in topological insulators.

name: Spin is a projective representation of SO(3)
summary: Angular-momentum operators obey the su(2) algebra, whose irreducible representations give j = 0, 1/2, 1, …. Half-integer spin exists because SU(2) double-covers SO(3): a 2π rotation multiplies a spinor by −1, as seen in neutron interferometry.

name: BEC breaks U(1); Bogoliubov phonon is the Goldstone mode
summary: The condensate order parameter ψ = √n e^{iθ} breaks the global phase symmetry that goes with atom-number conservation. The gapless Bogoliubov sound mode is the Goldstone boson, and its sound speed sets the Landau critical velocity for superfluid flow.

name: Time crystals break time-translation symmetry
summary: Wilczek's (2012) equilibrium time crystal is ruled out by the Watanabe–Oshikawa no-go theorem. Instead, periodically driven many-body systems, which conserve quasienergy rather than energy, break the discrete Floquet time-translation symmetry and respond at a multiple nT of the drive period (typically 2T). Many-body localization, prethermalization or slow critical dynamics stabilize this order, which has been seen with trapped ions, NV centres and superconducting qubits.

name: The SI second is a caesium hyperfine frequency
summary: Since 1967 the second has been defined by the Cs ground-state hyperfine frequency, which the 2019 SI wording keeps as a fixed constant. The metre is traced to the second through the fixed value of c. Optical lattice and ion clocks now beat Cs fountains by about 100× (~10⁻¹⁸ vs ~10⁻¹⁶), so the CIPM roadmap foresees an optical redefinition around 2030.

name: Unitary Fermi gas: universality from a missing scale
summary: At a Feshbach resonance the scattering length diverges and drops out, leaving density (and T/T_F) as the only scales. Dimensional analysis then makes observables universal functions times their free-Fermi-gas values; the Bertsch parameter ξ is the T=0 example. Dilute neutron matter, with a ≈ −18.5 fm, is approximately in the same universality class.

name: AMO measurements determine α and m_e for CODATA
summary: The fine-structure constant comes from atom-recoil interferometry (h/m for Cs and Rb) and from the Penning-trap electron g-factor combined with QED. These AMO inputs dominate the CODATA values of α, R∞ and m_e, and the ~5σ gap between the Cs and Rb values remains unresolved.

name: Clock ratios test the constancy of α and m_p/m_e
summary: Different transitions depend on α and μ = m_p/m_e with different sensitivities, so repeated ratios between clocks (Al+/Hg+, Yb+ E3/E2, Cs/Sr) bound present-day drifts at the ~10^{-18} per year level. The same ratios search for ultralight dark matter, which would make the constants oscillate.

name: Hydrogen spectroscopy, R∞ and the proton radius
summary: The Rydberg constant and the proton charge radius are fitted together to hydrogen and deuterium transition frequencies. The muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift (2010) gave a radius 4% smaller. The puzzle eased once newer hydrogen measurements and CODATA 2018/2022 moved to about 0.84 fm.

name: MCMC and nested sampling for GW source parameters
summary: Posteriors over the ~15 parameters of a quasi-circular spinning binary black hole are sampled with Markov-chain Monte Carlo (Metropolis–Hastings lineage, e.g. LALInference) and with Skilling's nested sampling (e.g. dynesty in Bilby); nested sampling also yields the Bayesian evidence used for model selection and tests of GR.

name: Monte Carlo over geometries: causal dynamical triangulations
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations define the gravitational path integral as a sum over causal simplicial geometries, Wick-rotated and sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo as in lattice field theory; simulations find a phase with an extended de Sitter-like 4D geometry whose spectral dimension runs from ~4 at large scales to ~2 at short scales.

name: String worldsheets as Riemann surfaces
summary: Perturbative string amplitudes are integrals over moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces; worldsheet conformal invariance makes the theory a 2D CFT, worked with holomorphic functions, contour-integral operator product expansions and modular invariance of the torus amplitude.

name: Retarded Green's function yields the quadrupole formula
summary: In Lorenz gauge, linearized gravity is a sourced wave equation for the trace-reversed perturbation; the same retarded Green's function as in electrodynamics gives the far-zone field and hence the quadrupole formula for gravitational radiation.
breaks: Valid only for weak fields and slow sources; nonlinear strong-field mergers need post-Newtonian or numerical-relativity methods.
